Retail chargeback software works by automating the dispute lifecycle, specifically targeting first-party fraud and delivery disputes. The platform gathers retail-specific evidence, such as proof of delivery and transaction history, to validate legitimate purchases. This technology submits data-driven responses to banks, effectively recovering revenue that would otherwise be lost due to buyer's remorse or confusion. What is first-party fraud and why is it such a problem for online retailers? First-party fraud, AKA friendly fraud or first-party misuse, is when your actual customer disputes a charge they legitimately made. Maybe they forgot about the purchase, didn't recognize the billing descriptor, or simply changed their mind and found a chargeback easier than a return. Unlike stolen card fraud, these people did order from you, did receive the product, and still filed a dispute. It's maddening because you did nothing wrong. Justt helps by pulling the evidence that proves the transaction was legitimate: delivery confirmation to the customer's address, their purchase history with you, IP matching, and any communications where they acknowledged receipt. Banks need to see proof the customer got what they paid for, and Justt builds that case automatically. A customer claims they never received their order, but tracking shows it was delivered. Can Justt help me win that dispute? This is one of the most common eCommerce disputes, and yes, it's winnable with the right evidence. Tracking data alone isn't always enough. Banks want to see delivery confirmation to the cardholder's address, signature if available, photo proof of delivery, and ideally a match between the shipping address and billing address. Justt connects with your logistics providers to pull this documentation automatically and formats it according to what each card network requires. Tickets are time-sensitive, high-emotion purchases. Someone buys floor seats on impulse, regrets the price two days later, and files a dispute instead of dealing with your refund policy. Plans change, the event sells out, and suddenly they "don't recognize" the charge. Secondary market transactions add another wrinkle: buyers claim tickets were fake or never delivered, even when scans prove otherwise. Justt pulls delivery confirmations, venue scan data, and event records to prove the ticket was real and used. A customer attended the event. Their ticket was scanned at the venue. Can they still win a chargeback? They try. And without the right evidence, they sometimes succeed. Banks don't automatically know your ticket was scanned at the door. You need to show that chain clearly: delivery confirmation to their email, the scan timestamp at the venue matching the event date, and any communications where they acknowledged receipt. Justt compiles this documentation automatically and formats it so dispute analysts can follow the logic without understanding how ticketing platforms work. How do I fight ticket chargebacks from secondary market purchases? Secondary transactions are messy because the original buyer and the person who attended are often different people. The cardholder claims fraud, but someone used that ticket at the show. Winning these disputes requires connecting the dots: proof the ticket was delivered to the purchaser's email, transfer records if it was resold through your platform, and scan confirmation showing the ticket was valid and used.
